newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to liberalise electricity sector - Potanin.
newsitem.headline: Russia to liberalise electricity sector - Potanin.

text.p: The Russian government has agreed to liberalise its electricity market, a former senior cabinet official said on Tuesday, in a step that could pave the way for big changes to natural monopolies.

Outgoing First Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the economy Vladimir Potanin told a news conference the government had agreed to create a wholesale electricity market and competition by making power generators independent.

"An important decision in principle has been taken on the liberalisation of the electricity market and on the creation of a wholesale market and a competitive environment by making generators independent companies," he said.
National power grid operator Unified Energy System of Russia currently controls the generation, transmission and distribution of nearly all electricity.
"The most important thing is that there is an understanding that it is necessary to have an independent operator on the electricity market," Potanin said.
The International Monetary Fund wants Moscow to make UES's central dispatching network, or generators, separate from its other units, as part of its $10 billion loan to Russia.
RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) is 52.5 percent state owned. Foreign investors collectively own a 22.5 percent stake.
